notes: OpenObserve creates its root user on the first start from ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL (the admin email you enter) and ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD (a generated password shown on the first-run card). Sign in with that email and password. The same email and password also work as HTTP basic auth for the ingestion API (POST https://<your domain>/api/default/<stream>/_json). Once the root user exists these variables no longer change it: change the password in the web interface instead.

ROOT_PASSWORD is a complex secret (letters, digits and one symbol from !@#%^*-_=+): OpenObserve refuses to start with a root password that lacks an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit or a special character ('ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD is too weak'), which a letters-and-digits password does not satisfy. In curl, quote the user:password pair (-u 'email:password').

Single-node mode as in the official quick start: one container, all data (the metadata database, the write-ahead log and the stored Parquet files) on local disk in one named volume on /data. There is no object storage and no cluster; OpenObserve's high-availability mode needs S3-compatible storage and is a different deployment.

The image is the official one from AWS ECR Public (public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/openobserve, the registry the installation docs name), pinned to v1.0.4 (the image openobserve/openobserve on Docker Hub is the same build).

ZO_WEB_URL is the site's address (used for links and the allowed browser origin) and follows the domain. ZO_COOKIE_SECURE_ONLY keeps the session cookie on HTTPS; ZO_TELEMETRY is off so the server does not report usage to the vendor.
OpenObserve sizes its in-memory caches from the container's memory limit, so the memory floor of 1g is a starting point: give it more if you ingest a lot or keep long time ranges in dashboards.

Data is kept until you set a retention: by default streams keep data indefinitely and the volume grows with what you ingest. Set the stream retention in the stream settings (or ZO_COMPACT_DATA_RETENTION_DAYS) for anything with real volume.
